Acute Appendicitis.scope: Adult assessment and surgical referral only; reconcile the 2025 WSES guideline before approving a definitive antibiotic or operative protocol.
actions: Arrange prompt surgical assessment, analgesia and fluid support according to clinical need.
Discuss operative care or selected nonoperative care with the surgical team; document selection criteria and recurrence risk.

Acute Bowel Obstruction.scope: Small-bowel obstruction only; do not generalise adhesive-obstruction observation thresholds to all bowel obstruction.
actions: Obtain early surgical review and assess for peritonitis, strangulation or ischaemia.
Use bowel rest, intravenous fluid and electrolyte correction and indicated decompression; deterioration requires urgent reassessment for surgery.

Acute Coronary Syndrome.scope: Adult ACS; NICE and US ACS prescribing branches must remain separate. Full antithrombotic, renal and bleeding-risk reconciliation remains pending.
actions: Give a single 300 mg aspirin loading dose when indicated and not contraindicated under the NICE ACS pathway.
Activate reperfusion assessment for STEMI; use a bleeding-risk and coronary-strategy-specific antithrombotic plan for NSTEMI rather than a universal P2Y12 or heparin regimen.

Acute Coronary Syndrome Assessment and E.scope: Adult ACS escalation; inherited investigation text is not newly verified.
actions: Activate the specialist reperfusion pathway for STEMI without waiting for a routine serial-troponin rule-out schedule.
For NSTEMI, assess bleeding risk and suitability and timing of coronary angiography before selecting antithrombotic treatment.

Acute Exacerbation of COPD.scope: NICE adult exacerbation branch. The inherited 40 mg steroid regimen is a different guideline approach and is not the NICE regimen. Antibiotic eligibility is not restricted to an ONLY cardinal-symptom rule.
actions: Under NICE NG115, the oral prednisolone course is 30 mg once daily for 5 days; assess contraindications and local prescribing requirements.

Use NG114 to consider antibiotics from sputum change, severity, admission history, cultures and resistance risk; reassess blood gases and provide NIV for persistent hypercapnic ventilatory failure despite optimal treatment.

Acute Heart Failure and Pulmonary Oedema.scope: Adult acute heart failure; prescriptions and ventilation require patient-specific specialist review.
actions: Use intravenous diuresis with renal function, weight and urine-output monitoring for congestion.
Avoid routine opiates, nitrates and inotropes; reserve ventilatory or vasoactive support for the specific clinical indications described in CG187.

Acute Ischemic Stroke.scope: Adult stroke; thrombolysis exclusions, post-thrombolysis antiplatelet timing and thrombectomy selection require stroke-team confirmation.
actions: Record last-known-well time and obtain urgent brain imaging; assess eligible patients for thrombolysis and thrombectomy.
Exclude intracranial haemorrhage before aspirin; do not apply the aspirin pathway without checking whether thrombolysis or another contraindication changes timing.

Acute Kidney Injury.scope: AKI assessment and escalation, not a dialysis prescription.
actions: Compare creatinine with baseline, track urine output and review hypovolaemia, obstruction and nephrotoxic exposure.
Request urgent ultrasound when cause is unknown or obstruction is suspected; seek immediate specialist advice for refractory electrolyte, acid-base, uraemic or fluid complications.

Acute Pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis; severity, fluids and necrosis decisions require specialist review.
actions: Avoid prophylactic antibiotics and routine fasting; identify a specific clinical reason before withholding oral intake.
For moderately severe or severe disease, start enteral nutrition within 72 hours and discuss infected necrosis with the specialist team.

Acute Poisoning and Overdose.scope: NG225 covers self-harm assessment, not antidote selection, toxic doses or general poisoning treatment. Agent-specific toxicology evidence remains required.
actions: For intentional overdose, arrange psychosocial assessment alongside physical care.
Obtain agent-specific poison-centre or toxicology advice; do not use this NICE self-harm source as an antidote or decontamination protocol.

Acute Severe Asthma Exacerbation.locator: Scope; chronic management and supported self-management
Acute Severe Asthma Exacerbation.scope: NG245 excludes acute attacks and severe asthma management. An acute BTS/SIGN or equivalent locally reviewed emergency pathway remains required.
actions: Escalate severe or life-threatening attacks through the emergency respiratory pathway; NG245 must not be cited as the acute rescue-treatment source.
After recovery, check controller treatment, inhaler technique and the written action plan using the chronic-management recommendations.

Acute Severe Asthma Exacerbation (Adult).locator: Scope; chronic management and supported self-management
Acute Severe Asthma Exacerbation (Adult).scope: NG245 is a chronic-management comparator only; it cannot verify emergency bronchodilator, steroid or magnesium doses.
actions: Use the locally reviewed acute-asthma emergency pathway for rescue treatment and escalation.
Before discharge, arrange controller review, inhaler-technique assessment and an individual written action plan; verify the acute prescribing source separately.

Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.scope: Adult acute UGIB; distinguish variceal from non-variceal treatment.
actions: Calculate the Blatchford score initially and arrange endoscopy immediately after resuscitation for unstable severe bleeding, or within 24 hours for other patients.
Do not routinely give acid suppression before endoscopy for suspected non-variceal bleeding under this NICE pathway; use a separate variceal pathway when suspected.

Adult Essential Hypertension Screening a.scope: NICE diagnosis thresholds; local Saudi risk tools and treatment implementation require review.
actions: Confirm clinic readings of 140/90 to below 180/120 mmHg using ABPM, or HBPM if ABPM is unsuitable.
Use a daytime ABPM or HBPM average of at least 135/85 mmHg to confirm hypertension with raised clinic pressure; assess severe readings for same-day referral indications.

Adult Periodic Health Examination.scope: Cardiovascular prevention component only; no single NICE guideline verifies the entire Saudi preventive-screening schedule.
actions: Separate asymptomatic prevention from symptoms needing diagnostic assessment.
Assess cardiovascular risk with a locally appropriate tool; verify cancer, infection and vaccination schedules against current Saudi policy individually.

Adult Vaccination Review.scope: Vaccine uptake only; NG218 does not supply an adult vaccine product/dose schedule, and CDC schedules are not automatically Saudi schedules.
actions: Check reliable immunisation records, eligibility and individual contraindications before planning catch-up.
Use current Saudi vaccine schedules and product guidance for intervals and doses; address uptake barriers and informed consent.

Advanced COPD Supportive Care.scope: Advanced COPD supportive care, not an opioid or home-oxygen prescribing protocol.
actions: Address breathlessness, function and advance-care preferences alongside respiratory treatment.
Coordinate respiratory, rehabilitation and palliative support; verify drug and oxygen decisions separately.

Advanced Dementia and Comfort-Focused Ca.scope: Advanced dementia; feeding and treatment goals require shared decisions.
actions: Support eating and drinking and assess swallowing concerns with speech and language input.
Avoid routine enteral feeding in severe dementia unless a potentially reversible comorbidity provides a specific indication; agree anticipatory and palliative plans.

Advanced Heart Failure Supportive Care.scope: Heart-failure symptom support alongside disease-modifying care.
actions: Review symptom burden and discuss palliative support according to need and preferences.
Coordinate the heart-failure team, primary care and palliative services; do not use a prognostic score alone to restrict access to supportive care.

Antenatal Care for Uncomplicated Pregnan.scope: Uncomplicated antenatal care; local screening availability requires adaptation.
actions: Arrange timely booking, explain the antenatal schedule and review medical, obstetric and psychosocial risks.
Assess blood pressure, fetal growth and movement concerns at the recommended contacts, and move to a specialist pathway if complications develop.

Asthma.scope: Chronic asthma; age-specific treatment must remain distinct from acute attacks.
actions: Confirm a compatible clinical history with objective testing; account for the effect of existing inhaled steroid treatment on results.
For newly diagnosed asthma at age 12 or over, consider the NICE as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol AIR branch, with locally licensed products and a written action plan.

Atrial Fibrillation [Adapted from NICE].scope: Adult AF; anticoagulation and cardioversion need individual assessment.
actions: Confirm AF on a 12-lead ECG, using ambulatory monitoring when episodes are intermittent.
Assess stroke and bleeding risks and discuss appropriate anticoagulation; do not substitute aspirin monotherapy for indicated stroke prevention.

Breast Cancer Management.scope: Early and locally advanced disease only; advanced breast cancer requires CG81 and current technology-appraisal review. The 2018 Saudi source alone cannot verify current systemic treatment.
actions: Confirm diagnosis, stage, receptor profile and fitness before multidisciplinary treatment planning.
Select surgery, radiotherapy and systemic treatment by stage and biomarkers; check current recommendations and local oncology access rather than adopting a historical drug list.

Breast Cancer Screening Discussion.scope: Familial-risk surveillance only; population screening ages and intervals require current Saudi programme evidence.
actions: Assess family history and eligibility for genetics or enhanced surveillance.
Discuss benefits and harms; do not extrapolate familial-risk surveillance schedules to all asymptomatic adults.

Cancer Pain Assessment and Support.locator: Starting strong opioids; breakthrough pain; adverse effects
Cancer Pain Assessment and Support.scope: Adult strong-opioid support; complete oncology pain and renal-dose review remains required.
actions: Discuss strong-opioid benefits, adverse effects and the plan for breakthrough pain when indicated.
Review constipation, nausea and sedation; seek specialist advice for significant renal or hepatic impairment before choosing or adjusting an opioid.

Cardiovascular Risk Assessment.scope: UK risk-estimation recommendations require local validation for Saudi use.
actions: Review smoking, blood pressure, lipids, diabetes, renal disease and family history before discussing absolute risk.
Choose a locally appropriate risk tool and discuss prevention benefits, harms and preferences rather than relying on a single laboratory result.
Base referral on the effect on vision and quality of life and the person's preferences, rather than a fixed visual-acuity cutoff.
Complete appropriate biometry and discuss procedure-specific benefits, risks and refractive expectations.

Cervical Cancer Screening and Follow-Up.scope: Suspected-cancer referral, not a population HPV screening schedule.
actions: Assess symptoms or an abnormal-appearing cervix through the appropriate diagnostic and suspected-cancer pathway.
Verify screening eligibility, HPV testing intervals and abnormal-result follow-up using the current Saudi screening programme; symptomatic assessment is separate.

Childhood Immunisation and Catch-Up.locator: Identifying eligible people; barriers to uptake
Childhood Immunisation and Catch-Up.scope: Uptake and access only; paediatric catch-up intervals and vaccine contraindications require Saudi product/schedule sources.
actions: Reconcile reliable vaccination records and identify missed eligible immunisations.
Use the current Saudi age-specific catch-up schedule, with consent and contraindication checks; do not infer dose intervals from this uptake guideline.
Use eGFR and urine ACR together, confirming persistence rather than diagnosing CKD from one abnormal result.
Stratify progression and cardiovascular risk; review nephrotoxic medicines, blood pressure and specialist-referral criteria.

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.scope: Stable adult COPD; acute exacerbation treatment is a separate branch.
actions: Confirm COPD using post-bronchodilator spirometry with an appropriate exposure and symptom history.
Review inhaler technique, smoking cessation, vaccination and pulmonary rehabilitation; individualise inhaled treatment and oxygen eligibility.

Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis and Treatmen.scope: Confirmed colorectal malignancy; molecular testing and systemic treatments need current specialist reconciliation.
actions: Complete diagnosis and staging and distinguish colon from rectal cancer before MDT planning.
Discuss stage-specific surgery, radiotherapy or systemic treatment with the colorectal MDT and address supportive-care needs.

Colorectal Cancer Screening.scope: Symptomatic referral only; diagnostic FIT recommendations do not define population-screening ages or intervals.
actions: Keep symptomatic colorectal investigation separate from an asymptomatic screening offer.
Use current Saudi screening eligibility and follow-up; a low FIT result must not override persistent concerning symptoms or clinical judgement.

Community-Acquired Pneumonia.scope: Current NICE pneumonia guidance, replacing reliance on older pneumonia guidance alone; local antibiotic selection remains required.
actions: Use clinical judgement with CRB65 in primary care or CURB65 in hospital to assess severity and place of care.
Choose prompt severity-appropriate antibiotics after allergy and local-resistance review; reassess clinical stability and course length.

Conservative Kidney Care Planning.scope: Shared renal replacement versus conservative-care decisions.
actions: Discuss conservative care and renal replacement with expected burdens, benefits and the person's priorities.
Provide an active symptom, nutrition and advance-care plan with clear ownership; revisit decisions as circumstances change.

Deep-Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embol.scope: Nonpregnant adult suspected/confirmed VTE; pregnancy requires a separate source.
actions: Use the relevant two-level Wells pathway with D-dimer and timely imaging; consider interim anticoagulation when testing is delayed and clinically appropriate.
Select treatment after reviewing bleeding risk, renal function, cancer, interactions and instability; escalate haemodynamically unstable PE urgently.

Delirium and Agitation Near End of Life.scope: Last-days-of-life distress only; delirium outside this setting requires CG103 assessment.
actions: Look for reversible causes of distress and use supportive measures.
Individualise symptom treatment and seek specialist advice for diagnostic uncertainty or persistent agitation.

Diabetes Screening in At-Risk Adults.locator: Risk identification; blood testing; intensive lifestyle change
Diabetes Screening in At-Risk Adults.scope: Type 2 diabetes risk detection; not a symptomatic DKA pathway.
actions: Use risk assessment to select appropriate HbA1c or fasting-glucose testing and confirm diagnostic results when required.
Offer intensive lifestyle support and follow-up to people at high risk, using locally validated risk tools and eligibility.

Diabetic Ketoacidosis.scope: Adult DKA; an up-to-date local DKA protocol must specify fluid, insulin and potassium dosing and resolution criteria.
actions: Measure ketones, acid-base status and electrolytes and identify the precipitating cause; seek trained acute diabetes support.
Use protocolised isotonic fluid, intravenous insulin and monitored potassium replacement; bicarbonate is not routine, and glucose-containing fluid permits continued ketone clearance.

Dyslipidaemia and Atherosclerotic Risk.locator: Lipid modification; primary and secondary prevention
Dyslipidaemia and Atherosclerotic Risk.scope: Risk-based lipid therapy, with local formulary and pregnancy review.
actions: Assess full lipid profile, secondary causes, cardiovascular history and overall risk.
Discuss appropriate statin-based prevention and monitor response and adverse effects; distinguish primary from secondary prevention.

Elective Coronary Revascularisation Revi.scope: Stable angina; this source does not replace an ACS pathway.
actions: Review symptom control and optimal medical treatment before considering elective revascularisation.
Use a multidisciplinary discussion of coronary anatomy, comorbidity and preferences to choose between PCI, surgery and continued medical treatment.

Elective Hernia Repair Assessment.scope: Preoperative tests only; hernia-specific indication, approach and mesh decisions need a separate surgical source.
actions: Select preoperative tests by procedure, comorbidity and ASA status rather than a blanket panel.
Confirm a separate hernia-specific surgical plan and assess emergency symptoms before proceeding with elective care.
Discuss alternatives, expected recovery and procedure-specific risks with the patient.
Provide preoperative rehabilitation and coordinate anaesthesia, analgesia, postoperative rehabilitation and locally reviewed thromboprophylaxis.

Elective Hysterectomy for Benign Disease.scope: Heavy menstrual bleeding only; other benign indications require their own evidence.
actions: Confirm the indication and discuss medical and uterus-preserving alternatives when appropriate.
Discuss fertility, ovarian function, complications and the route of hysterectomy before an informed decision.

Elective Valve Intervention Assessment.scope: Adult valve disease; thresholds vary by lesion and patient factors.
actions: Obtain echocardiographic characterisation and specialist review when intervention is being considered.
Discuss surgical versus transcatheter options with the valve team using symptoms, severity, ventricular function, risk and preferences.

Fetal Growth Restriction Assessment.scope: Detection and referral only; Doppler surveillance and delivery thresholds for established FGR require a specialist obstetric source.
actions: Review growth-risk factors and measured growth; arrange ultrasound when growth is concerning.
Refer suspected restriction for specialist assessment and document movement concerns; do not infer a Doppler or delivery protocol from routine antenatal guidance.

Heart Failure.scope: Chronic heart failure; therapy is determined by phenotype and comorbidity.
actions: Use natriuretic peptide testing and echocardiography to establish diagnosis and cardiac phenotype.
Review current phenotype-specific disease-modifying treatment with the specialist team, including renal function, potassium, blood pressure and congestion monitoring.

Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State.scope: NG28 is longitudinal diabetes guidance, not a complete HHS resuscitation protocol. HHS-specific osmolality, fluid and insulin targets remain unverified.
actions: Escalate suspected HHS to the acute diabetes team and obtain an approved HHS-specific protocol.
Do not copy DKA fluid, insulin or biochemical-resolution targets into HHS without HHS-specific evidence.

Hypertension in Adults [Adapted from NIC.scope: Adult nonpregnant hypertension; risk tools and formulary require Saudi adaptation.
actions: Confirm elevated clinic pressure with ABPM or HBPM and evaluate target-organ injury and cardiovascular risk.
Individualise treatment by age, comorbidity and frailty; severe pressure with retinal or life-threatening organ findings warrants same-day assessment.

Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy.scope: Maternal hypertensive disease; specialist monitoring and gestational-age decisions are required.
actions: Assess maternal symptoms, pressure, renal/liver function and platelets alongside fetal wellbeing.
Escalate severe disease; use pregnancy-specific antihypertensive and magnesium pathways and senior obstetric review of delivery timing.

Hypothyroidism.scope: Primary adult hypothyroidism; pregnancy, central hypothyroidism and myxoedema need separate specialist pathways.
actions: Use TSH with reflex FT4 for suspected primary disease, and TSH plus FT4 when pituitary disease is suspected; ask about biotin interference.
Use levothyroxine first line, with lower initial dosing in older adults or cardiovascular disease and TSH-guided follow-up; do not routinely use liothyronine or natural thyroid extract.

Intrapartum Fetal Compromise.scope: Intrapartum fetal monitoring; interpretation must include the whole clinical context.
actions: Interpret CTG features together with contractions, maternal condition and evolving intrapartum risk.
Obtain urgent obstetric review for concerning traces; correct reversible causes and assess whether expedited birth is needed.

Ischaemic Heart Disease.scope: Stable angina only; new or unstable symptoms require the ACS pathway.
actions: Review symptom pattern, risk reduction and suitable anti-anginal treatment.
Discuss revascularisation when symptoms remain inadequately controlled and assess anatomy and patient preferences with the specialist team.

Kidney Failure Planning and Dialysis Acc.scope: Preparation and shared decisions, not a dialysis initiation prescription.
actions: Plan renal replacement or conservative care in advance through shared decisions about modalities and goals.
Coordinate access preparation with the chosen modality and likely timing; integrate symptom, nutritional and psychosocial support.

Last Days of Life Care.scope: Adults thought to be in the final days; prognosis remains uncertain and requires reassessment.
actions: Explain uncertainty and agree an individual care plan with the person and those important to them.
Reassess comfort, hydration and anticipatory medication needs, balancing benefit and burden.

Lung Cancer Management.scope: Stage-specific lung cancer management; modern molecular and systemic options cannot be verified solely from a 2019 local guideline.
actions: Complete histology, stage, fitness and appropriate molecular testing before thoracic MDT decisions.
Check current stage- and biomarker-specific treatments and supportive-care options; verify each systemic regimen through the current oncology protocol.

Malignant Bowel Obstruction Support.scope: Last-days-of-life nausea support only; complete malignant-obstruction surgical, decompression and antisecretory treatment evidence remains required.
actions: Assess whether obstruction and potentially reversible causes explain nausea.
Agree comfort goals and seek specialist advice on symptom control and intervention burden.

Maternal Sepsis in Pregnancy or Postpart.scope: Pregnant or recently pregnant people; do not transfer the NG253 general-adult fluid algorithm automatically.
actions: Use pregnancy-specific risk assessment and urgent senior obstetric review; high-risk suspected sepsis needs prompt antibiotics and source assessment.
Follow NG255 for resuscitation and reassess after each fluid bolus; integrate maternal and fetal monitoring and source control.

Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Evaluati.locator: Surgical referral; preoperative assessment; postoperative follow-up
Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Evaluati.scope: Adult bariatric evaluation; eligibility and long-term care require local adaptation.
actions: Assess eligibility and suitability through a multidisciplinary medical, nutritional and psychological review.
Discuss procedure-specific risks and lifelong nutritional monitoring, supplementation and follow-up before surgery.

Nausea and Vomiting in Advanced Illness.scope: Last-days-of-life symptoms only; broader advanced-illness antiemetic selection needs another source.
actions: Assess likely cause, including medicines and obstruction, alongside goals of care.
Individualise symptom treatment and seek specialist advice if symptoms persist or diagnosis is uncertain.

Obesity and Weight-Related Health.locator: Identifying and assessing overweight, obesity and central adiposity
Obesity and Weight-Related Health.scope: Adult assessment; medicine eligibility and surgery are separately specified chapters.
actions: Assess BMI, central adiposity, related conditions and the person's goals without stigma.
Offer appropriate behavioural and multidisciplinary support and verify eligibility for medicines or surgery in the current guidance and local formulary.

Osteoarthritis and Chronic Pain.scope: Osteoarthritis-specific care, not all chronic pain syndromes.
actions: Use clinical diagnosis for typical osteoarthritis and avoid routine imaging unless atypical features suggest another diagnosis.
Prioritise tailored therapeutic exercise and weight management where relevant; choose analgesia according to joint, risks and response.

Osteoporosis Risk Assessment and Fractur.scope: Use current NG259 rather than superseded CG146; drug-treatment selection requires its own current evidence.
actions: Assess fragility-fracture risk with clinical risk factors and an appropriate validated risk tool.
Use the current NG259 criteria for further assessment and discuss prevention and referral; do not treat an old CG146 link as current guidance.

Postpartum Haemorrhage Response.scope: Obstetric haemorrhage emergency; uterotonic contraindications and escalation require the full local protocol.
actions: Activate obstetric haemorrhage support, resuscitate and assess the cause while monitoring blood loss and maternal condition.
Select uterotonics considering prior prophylaxis and contraindications; add tranexamic acid under the emergency protocol and escalate ongoing bleeding.

Preconception Health and Risk Review.scope: Nutrition and folate component only; diabetes and other conditions require their separate preconception pathways.
actions: Review nutrition, folic-acid eligibility, medicines and existing conditions before pregnancy.
Use condition-specific specialist planning, including NG3 for diabetes, rather than applying a single universal preconception treatment schedule.

Prelabour Rupture of Membranes.scope: Preterm rupture; term rupture requires NG235 and neonatal-infection guidance.
actions: Confirm suspected preterm membrane rupture with the recommended assessment and evaluate infection, gestational age and fetal wellbeing.
Use the P-PROM prophylaxis pathway when indicated; co-amoxiclav is not recommended for this purpose. Keep term and preterm management distinct.

Preterm Labour and Threatened Preterm Bi.scope: Gestational-age-specific care; full dose and exclusion review remains required.
actions: Assess suspected labour and membrane status, using appropriate diagnostic testing and obstetric review.
Check gestational-age eligibility and contraindications for tocolysis, antenatal steroids and magnesium neuroprotection, and plan appropriate place of birth.

Progressive Neurological Disease Support.scope: Motor neurone disease only; this must not be generalised to every progressive neurological diagnosis.
actions: For MND, coordinate communication, nutrition, mobility and respiratory assessment through the specialist MDT.
Discuss anticipatory and end-of-life preferences; obtain a disease-specific source for other neurological disorders.

Prostate Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment.scope: Suspected and confirmed prostate cancer; current systemic options require oncology review.
actions: Discuss multiparametric MRI and biopsy in the context of PSA, examination, comorbidity and suitability for radical treatment.
Use risk-stratified shared decisions about surveillance or treatment, explaining urinary, bowel and sexual effects.

Reduced Fetal Movements Assessment.scope: Recognition and immediate maternity assessment; further CTG/ultrasound thresholds require specialist protocols.
actions: Advise prompt contact with maternity services for concerns about reduced movements after 24 weeks.
Assess the woman and baby; do not replace assessment with a routine home movement-counting package.

Sepsis.scope: People aged 16 or over who are not pregnant or recently pregnant; NG254 and NG255 are separate populations.
actions: Use the current risk-based sepsis pathway with clinical judgement, urgent senior review and timely antibiotics for high-risk illness.

When fluid resuscitation is indicated, NG253 starts with 250 ml crystalloid, reassesses each bolus and seeks senior advice if response is inadequate after 1000 ml; do not automatically apply this to pregnancy.

Severe Hypoglycaemia.scope: Adult hypoglycaemia, with an acute local treatment protocol required.
actions: Treat promptly using the appropriate route for consciousness and swallowing safety; recheck glucose and clinical response.
Review recurrence risks, insulin or drug exposure and hypoglycaemia awareness; provide prevention education and follow-up.

Tobacco and Nicotine Cessation.scope: Tobacco cessation; pregnancy and age-specific restrictions require separate checks.
actions: Offer behavioural support and discuss suitable cessation aids with contraindication and local-licensing checks.
Agree a quit plan and follow-up, reviewing adherence, adverse effects and relapse support.

Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Longitudinal Ca.scope: February 2026 NICE update; local prescribing, sick-day rules and contraindications remain required.
actions: Choose initial treatment using the current comorbidity-specific recommendations and individual goals.
For adults without relevant comorbidity, the 2026 NICE branch offers modified-release metformin plus an SGLT2 inhibitor; verify renal, pregnancy and ketoacidosis precautions and local availability.

Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy and.locator: Pregnant women and women who gave birth or had miscarriage or termination in the past 6 weeks
Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy and.scope: Hospital thromboprophylaxis only; NG89 does not verify the complete diagnosis or treatment of pregnancy-associated VTE.
actions: Assess pregnancy-specific thrombosis and bleeding risk for prophylaxis when hospitalised.
For suspected or confirmed VTE, obtain a dedicated obstetric diagnostic and therapeutic anticoagulation source and specialist review; do not import the nonpregnant DOAC pathway.
